title: Strict residue and completion reduction in the proof of Epp
statement: Let $A\to B$ be an injective local map of discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction fields $K\subseteq L$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Suppose $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ is perfect of characteristic $p>0$ (Frobenius is surjective). Put $l=B/\mathfrak m_B$ and $l_{\mathrm{perf}}=\bigcap_{n\geq0}\{x^{p^n}:x\in l\}$. Assume every element of $l_{\mathrm{perf}}$ is separable algebraic over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Fix a uniformizer $\pi$ of $A$. For any injective local map $U\to V$ of discrete valuation rings, with fraction fields $F\subseteq G$, call a finite field extension $H/F$ a weak solution if, writing $U_H$ for the integral closure of $U$ in $H$ and $V_H$ for that of $V$ in $(G\otimes_F H)_{\mathrm{red}}$, every maximal ideal $q$ of $V_H$ has maximal contraction $n=q\cap U_H$, both $(U_H)_n$ and $(V_H)_q$ are discrete valuation rings, and $n(V_H)_q=q(V_H)_q$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Here reduction means quotient by all nilpotents, finite means finite-dimensional over the base field, and local means pulling back the maximal ideal to the maximal ideal. There exists a commutative square of injective local maps $A\to A^{\prime}$, $B\to B^{\prime}$, $A^{\prime}\to B^{\prime}$ in which $A^{\prime}$ and $B^{\prime}$ are complete discrete valuation rings [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], the image $\pi^{\prime}$ of $\pi$ is a uniformizer of $A^{\prime}$, the residue field $k^{\prime}$ of $A^{\prime}$ is an algebraic closure of $k$, and, writing $l^{\prime}$ for the residue field of $B^{\prime}$, one has $k^{\prime}=\bigcap_{n\geq0}(l^{\prime})^{p^n}$ inside $l^{\prime}$. This square has the following descent property. Set $K^{\prime}=\operatorname{Frac}(A^{\prime})$. If $H/K^{\prime}$ is a finite weak solution for $A^{\prime}\to B^{\prime}$, and in characteristic $p$ it is the compositum of a finite separable extension of $K^{\prime}$ and $K^{\prime}[(\pi^{\prime})^{1/p^r}]$ for some $r\geq0$, then there exists a finite weak solution for $A\to B$. In characteristic zero of $K$ no extra condition on $H$ is required. A compositum here is the subfield generated by the two embedded extensions in a common field. The square is constructed without assuming that a weak solution exists.

source.place: Tag 09ET, lemma-solution-after-strict-henselization; Tag 09F9, theorem-epp, proof paragraphs from strict residue closures through completion, using Tag 09EJ, lemma-approximate-separable-extension and Tag 09ES, lemma-solutions-go-down. The prescribed uniformizer-root extension is retained in the equicharacteristic descent.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-strict-residue-square] to $A\to B$, obtaining $A_s\to B_s$ and its commutative square. Write $F=\operatorname{Frac}(A_s)$ and $G=\operatorname{Frac}(B_s)$. Its lower maximal-ideal equality makes the image $\pi_s$ of $\pi$ a uniformizer. Write $k_s,l_s$ for the new residue fields. They are separable closures of $k,l$. Since $k$ is perfect, an irreducible polynomial over $k$ cannot have zero derivative: otherwise all exponents are divisible by $p$, and taking $p$-th roots of its coefficients writes it as a $p$-th power. Thus all irreducible polynomials over $k$ are separable and its separable closure $k_s$ is an algebraic closure. Retain this square and its weak-solution descent for the final step.

source.place: Tag 09ET (lemma-solution-after-strict-henselization) and Tag 09F9 (theorem-epp), strict-residue paragraph; perfect lower residue specialization.

proof.text: Write $k_s\subseteq l_s$ for the residue fields of Step 1. Let $x\in\bigcap_n(l_s)^{p^n}$ and let $f$ be its minimal polynomial over $l$. Fix $n$ and $y\in l_s$ with $y^{p^n}=x$, and let $g$ be the minimal polynomial of $y$ over $l$. Then $l(x)\subseteq l(y)$, and $y$ is separable over $l(x)$ because it is separable over $l$; its minimal polynomial over $l(x)$ divides $T^{p^n}-x=(T-y)^{p^n}$ and has distinct roots, so it is $T-y$ and $l(y)=l(x)$. Raising the coefficients of $g$ to the $p^n$-th power gives a monic polynomial $g^{(p^n)}$ over $l$ of degree $[l(y):l]=[l(x):l]$ with $g^{(p^n)}(x)=g(y)^{p^n}=0$, hence $g^{(p^n)}=f$ and every coefficient of $f$ lies in $\{a^{p^n}:a\in l\}$. As $n$ is arbitrary, the coefficients of $f$ lie in $l_{\mathrm{perf}}$, so they are algebraic over $k$ by hypothesis and $x$ is algebraic over $k$. Since $k_s$ is an algebraically closed subfield of $l_s$ containing $k$, $x$ is algebraic over $k_s$ and therefore $x\in k_s$. Conversely $k_s$ is algebraically closed of characteristic $p$, so every element has a $p^n$-th root in $k_s$ for each $n$, and $k_s\subseteq\bigcap_n(l_s)^{p^n}$. The two inclusions give precisely $k_s=\bigcap_n(l_s)^{p^n}$.

source.place: Tag 09F9, strict-residue paragraph; the perfect-core inclusion is the argument of ILO, Expose IV, Lemma 3.2.2, printed pp.55-56, written out.

proof.text: Set $A'=\widehat{A_s}$ and $B'=\widehat{B_s}$, using maximal-ideal completion. Apply [lem-sfb-principal-regular-local-completion-dvr] to each DVR and a uniformizer. It gives complete DVRs with unchanged residue fields and maximal ideals generated by the images of those uniformizers; in particular $\pi'=\widehat\pi_s$ is a uniformizer of $A'$. The canonical maps are injective: by [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], a nonzero element is $ut^n$, whose component modulo $t^{n+1}$ is nonzero. To extend $A_s\to B_s$, write $\pi_s=u t^e$ in $B_s$ by the same lemma, where $e\geq1$ because the map is local. The quotient maps $A_s/(\pi_s^n)\to B_s/(t^n)$ are well defined and compatible, hence give $A'\to B'$ on compatible sequences. The equality $\pi'=u t^e$ still holds, with $u$ a unit. This map is local (units remain units and $\pi'$ maps into the maximal ideal) and injective (a nonzero kernel ideal in a DVR would contain a power of $\pi'$, whose image is nonzero). This constructs the required square without using any weak solution, and Step 2 proves its residue-core assertion.

source.place: Tag 09F9, completion square; algebra.tex Tag 0328 completion argument, in the existing principal-regular-local-completion node; componentwise construction written explicitly.

proof.text: Now suppose $H/K'$ is a finite weak solution with the stated characteristic-dependent condition, where $K'=\operatorname{Frac}(A')$. Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-completion-extension-approximation] to $A_s$, $\pi_s$ and $H$. In characteristic zero every finite field extension is separable; in characteristic $p$ the assumed compositum is exactly the other case of that lemma. Obtain a finite $N/F$ with $K'\otimes_FN\simeq H$. Write $R$ for the integral closure of $A_s$ in $N$, $S$ for the integral closure of $A'$ in $H$, and $T$ for the integral closure of $B'$ in $(\operatorname{Frac}(B')\otimes_F N)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Tensor associativity identifies this last reduced algebra with $(\operatorname{Frac}(B')\otimes_{K'}H)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Thus the weak-solution hypothesis concerns exactly $S\to T$, not a different normalized tensor algebra.

source.place: Tags 09EJ (lemma-approximate-separable-extension) and 09F9, completion-descent paragraph, retaining the same uniformizer roots.

proof.text: The completion map $A_s\to A'$ has maximal-ideal equality and identical residue fields by Step 3, so it satisfies every hypothesis of [lem-sfb-dvr-index-one-separable-base-change], with finite extension $N/F$. By Step 4, $(K'\otimes_F N)_{\mathrm{red}}=H$, so the unconditional local part of that node gives $nS_Q=QS_Q$ for every maximal ideal $Q$ of $S$, with $n=Q\cap R$ maximal. Its conditional global tensor-isomorphism assertion is not needed. For every maximal ideal $q$ of $T$, the weak-solution hypothesis on $H$, which by Step 4 concerns exactly $S\to T$, makes $Q=q\cap S$ maximal and gives $QT_q=qT_q$. Put $n=q\cap R=Q\cap R$. Then $nT_q=(nS_Q)T_q=QT_q=qT_q$. The maximal contractions and both DVR localizations for $R\to T$ are supplied by [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], finite case, applied to $A_s\to B'$ and $N/F$. Hence $N/F$ is a weak solution for $A_s\to B'$.

Let $C$ be the integral closure of $B_s$ in $D=(G\otimes_F N)_{\mathrm{red}}$, and put $G'=\operatorname{Frac}(B')$. There is an identification $(G'\otimes_F N)_{\mathrm{red}}=(G'\otimes_G D)_{\mathrm{red}}$: tensoring the quotient by the nilradical has kernel generated by tensors with a nilpotent second factor; every finite sum of such tensors is nilpotent, by expanding a power larger than the sum of their nilpotence exponents. Hence both quotients have the same reduction. For each field factor $E$ of $D$, the corresponding factor of $C$ is the integral closure of $B_s$ in $E$, and the corresponding factors of $T$ normalize $B'$ in $(G'\otimes_GE)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Given a maximal ideal $c$ of $C$, apply [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], finite case, to $B_s\to B'$ and this $E/G$. It supplies a maximal ideal $q$ of $T$ over $c$ and a DVR local map $C_c\to T_q$. Applying the same node to $A_s\to B_s$ and $N/F$ gives a maximal $n=c\cap R$ and a DVR $R_n$, mapping locally to $C_c$; then $n=q\cap R$. Write a uniformizer of $R_n$ as a unit times $t^a$ in $C_c$, and $t$ as a unit times $v^b$ in $T_q$, using [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power]. Both $a,b\geq1$. Step 5 says its image generates the maximal ideal of $T_q$, so $ab=1$ and $a=1$. Therefore $nC_c=cC_c$ for every $c$, and $N/F$ is a weak solution for $A_s\to B_s$.

source.place: Tag 09ES (lemma-solutions-go-down)(1), its normalized-branch argument expanded; Tag 09EM (remark-construction).

proof.text: Apply the descent assertion of [lem-sfb-dvr-strict-residue-square] to the weak solution $N/F$ from Step 6. It supplies a finite weak solution for the original $A\to B$, with all maximal contractions, DVR localizations and ideal equalities in the definition of weak solution. Together with the independently constructed square of Step 3 and the residue equality of Step 2, this proves every assertion of the item.
